newsitem.title: UK: Moody's says ups Greece's soveriegn ceiling rating.
newsitem.headline: Moody's says ups Greece's soveriegn ceiling rating.

text.p: Moody's Investors Service said on Monday it upgraded the sovereign ceilings for long-term foreign-currency bonds and bank deposits of Greece to Baa1 from Baa3.
"The sovereign ceiling for short-term notes and deposits was raised to Prime-2 from Prime-3," Moody's said.

The upgrade also covers rated foreign-currency-denominated bonds and notes issued by the Hellenic Republic, as well as outstanding rated issues of the Bank of Greece, which acted as agent for the government of the Hellenic Republic until January 1994.

Moody's said that the upgrades are triggered by the improvement in the fiscal balances in the past few years, as well as the stronger political resolve to continue with policies consistent with EU convergence.
"On the macroeconomic front, the economy has began expanding thanks to the robust growth of investment, both private and public," Moody's said in a statement.

It said industrial production has picked up and manufacturing employment has stopped falling. Inflation has been reduced to single digit levels, for the first time in two decades, and confidence has been established in the drachma.
